subject: Apex Financials - Azure Marketplace private SKU: seller-sourced amendment
messages:

Cc: Rajesh Iyer <rajesh.iy@apexfin.com>, procurement@apexfin.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood private SKU for Apex - next steps on amendment

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the engineering team was pleased with latency and isolation options. Procurement asked me to kick off the paperwork for the Azure private SKU (seller-sourced) we discussed. Attached is our standard MSA + procurement checklist. High-level asks from our side:

- 12-month committed spend with monthly invoicing cadence
- Data residency confirmed for US-East (we will require audit logs sent to our SIEM)
- A clause to limit liability tied to third-party cloud infra outages (we expect carve-outs for cloud provider downtime)
- Standard indemnity and IP language — our legal flagged an IP escrow request but said it might be negotiable if you can confirm model and weights handling.

Can you share Redwood's preferred amendment (seller-sourced private plan) and any standard redlines you accept? Also if you could confirm billing contact and a prelim commercial term sheet, that will help us move to SOW and PO.

Thanks,
Olivia Park
Head of Procurement
Apex Financials

Attachments: APX_MSA_standard.docx (docx), Apex_procurement_checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@apexfin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood private SKU for Apex - next steps on amendment

Hi Olivia —

Appreciate the clear list. We're excited to get Apex on a private plan in Azure East US. Quick notes and asks from our side before we circulate a seller-sourced amendment: 

- We'll start with a 12-month term; typical billing is monthly via invoice. I'll include finance's billing contact in a follow-up.
- Data residency and audit logs: Redwood can deliver audit logs to your SIEM via S3 push or shared Logstash endpoint — need to align on format and retention (we usually do 90 days by default; extensions available).
- Liability/force majeure: we can accept carve-outs for cloud provider outages but will retain a standard uptime SLA exclusion; Markus, can you summarize the legal position below?
- IP escrow: this is rarer for hosted/inference; our standard approach is to outline what we host vs what we share. If Apex requires escrow for weights, that will be an exception and we'll need a short call between legal teams to scope technical feasibility.

I'll attach a draft seller-sourced amendment and a term sheet showing pricing bands for committed spend and burst. For speed, our recommended path:
1) I send the seller-sourced amendment with our standard commercial redlines
2) Apex reviews and marks changes in the MSA redline
3) Legal sync (30m) to resolve major points (liability, IP, audit)
4) Finalize and send DocuSign

Proposed times: Thu 15 Jan 10:00-11:00 PT or Fri 16 Jan 09:00-10:00 PT for the legal sync. Which works for you?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
phone: +1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: azure_privatesku_term_sheet_20260112.pdf (pdf), seller_sourced_amendment_draft_v1.docx (docx)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Redwood private SKU for Apex - next steps on amendment

Vanessa/Ben —

Read through Apex's MSA and Olivia's notes. High-level legal summary for the call: 

1) Liability and force majeure: Acceptable to carve out cloud provider outage as a force majeure event. We should add explicit language limiting Redwood's liability to fees paid in prior 12 months for service interruptions caused solely by the cloud provider. Equivalent language used in other marketplace private plans.

2) Audit logs & data residency: We can agree to push logs to a customer-managed S3 endpoint. Need to confirm whether Apex requires logs to be retained beyond 1 year — that would be an ops cost add-on. Suggest we commit to 90 days included, 1 year for an extra fee.

3) IP escrow: Our standard position is no escrow for model weights. We can offer a technical attestation describing storage, access controls, and key management (KMS) for weights and model artifacts. If Apex insists, treat as an SEP (special exception) with cost recovery and a 3-way technical workshop.

4) Indemnity: Apex's proposed reciprocal indemnity is acceptable with some carve-outs. We should exclude claims arising from misuse by Apex (e.g., prompts that lead to IP infringement).

I'll prepare a clean redline of their MSA with suggested edits and a short memo for the legal sync. Keep the call to 30 minutes — focus on three buckets: liability, audit/logs, and IP.

-MK
Markus Klein
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

Attachment: APX_MSA_redline_v3.docx (docx)

From: Rajesh Iyer <rajesh.iy@apexfin.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Olivia Park <olivia.park@apexfin.com>
Cc: procurement@apexfin.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 11:09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood private SKU for Apex - next steps on amendment

Vanessa/Markus —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the redline. A few counterpoints from Apex legal before the call: 

- Limitation of liability: Apex cannot accept an overall cap that is lower than 12 months of fees. Our security team insists on a higher uplift if the incident results from negligent access controls. Could Redwood consider a tiered cap (12 months standard; higher for proven Redwood negligence)?

- Audit logs: We appreciate the S3 push option. Apex requires a signed SOC2 attestation for the calendar year prior to onboarding. Can you provide your SOC2 report and confirm the attestation will be current at signing?

- IP escrow: Rather than full escrow, our legal is open to a compromise: a scoped source-code escrow limited to the inference runtime and the deployment manifest (not model weights). This would be neutral and addresses our continuity concerns. If Redwood can accept a narrowly-scoped escrow with defined release triggers, we can avoid a lengthy workshop.

We're available for the 30-minute sync on Thu 22 Jan at 10:00 PT; if that works for your team we can lock it.

Regards,
Rajesh
Procurement Lead, Apex Financials

Attachments: Apex_amendment_comments.pdf (pdf)

Hi all —

Quick operational summary ahead of the Thu 22 call (10:00 PT):

- Finance/billing: billing contact is invoices@redwood.com, remit to Redwood Inference, PO must reference deal APX-4521. We'll accept monthly net-30 invoices; if Apex needs monthly POs let us know and we can route through our AR.
- SOC2: Redwood will share a redacted SOC2 Type II report and an attestation letter before the call. I will send the link to the secure folder shortly.
- Escrow: From an infra/ops perspective, a runtime-only escrow (no weights) looks feasible if release triggers are limited (acquirer insolvency or material breach after cure). We will need to scope the exact artifacts — Vanessa/Markus can capture that in the redline.
- Retention: Included audit push is 90 days. If Apex requires 1 year retention we'll provide pricing for extended retention; typical add is $0.02 per GB/month depending on volume.

Vanessa — locking the Thu 22 Jan 10:00 PT slot. I'll circulate the dial-in and the SOC2 link (secure) in a separate email.

Best,
